summary:
I've been chasing a nasty upgrade bug on Hermes-Agent, my personal AI assistant. A routine update jumped it 25,000 commits in one go and the tool-calling convention changed underneath it — MCP tool names went from single to double underscores. The failure mode was the interesting part: instead of erroring cleanly, the local model would see "not a deferrable tool," read that as "you're calling it wrong," and spiral into retries, inventing pseudo-XML tool syntax, compulsively writing memory notes to itself about how to fix it. Looked exactly like model stupidity. It wasn't — it just needed the right tool name. Swept 47 stale references across 13 files and it settled down.

That led me into a proper A/B test: benchmarking a second local model (GLM-4.7-Flash) against the incumbent brain to see if tool-selection reliability would improve. Stood it up as an additive route so I could compare without touching production. Both models scored a perfect 8/8 on my existing test harness, which told me less about the models than about my harness — it was built to catch an older, dumber failure and wasn't discriminating enough to reproduce the real problem I was seeing in production. That's the more useful result: knowing your test doesn't measure what you think it measures beats a clean pass/fail.

On BudgetTracker, my expense-tracking app, I've been building out a read-only MCP tool surface so Hermes can answer real financial questions — burn rate, spending anomalies, cash flow projections — using actual computed SQL rather than letting a model guess at arithmetic. Chasing that down turned up a couple of latent Postgres bugs that had been sitting dormant since a database migration, the kind that only surface the first time a new query path actually exercises them.

highlights.oneLiner: Chased a tool-naming upgrade regression that looked like model failure but wasn't
A/B'd a second local model against the incumbent; learned the test harness was the weak link
Building read-only MCP tools so queries use computed SQL, not model arithmetic
Surfaced latent Postgres bugs left over from a prior DB migration
